source: Game-owned gearbox catalogue (gearbox swap, 2026-10-13). One row per gearbox file the garage offers. What a physics_sim gearbox file cannot say lives here: display name, kind (manual | sequential | automatic | dual_clutch | cvt), focus (economy | touring | performance | race), gear_type (helical | straight_cut, the later gear-whine audio keys on it), synchro (cone | dog | none: the clutch-to-clutch kinds shift on wet clutches), the input torque rating and the card text. rating_nm is the maximum engine torque the box is rated for (N*m at the input shaft): physics_sim's GearboxDesc has no rating yet, so the rating is kept HERE and moves into the physics file when the physics session adds one; the garage offers a box only for an engine whose peak torque does not exceed it. All ratings and designs are invented [AS] and chosen to cover the shipped engines (engine peaks: i4 2.0 ~212, A25A 290, N52 300, R26B 608, hyper V8 1387 N*m). Paths are relative to the repository root. Automatic (torque converter) and dual_clutch rows (2026-10-16) also carry a 'tcu' object: the automatic_tcu fields that belong to the box; the engine-dependent shift, kickdown, lock-up and launch rpm points are derived from the installed engine on install (rg::derive_automatic_tcu_points). CVT rows (2026-10-16, physics_sim CVT plan C1) name physics_sim's push-belt sedan_cvt (torque converter) and sedan_cvt_clutch (starting clutch), rated 250 N*m = their files' rated_input_torque_nm; their 'tcu' adds 'cvt': {stepped_sport}, the variator's target-rpm and minimum-rpm curves are derived from the installed engine on install. A section without rows is listed as 'coming soon'; the kinds themselves are fixed in rg::GearboxCatalog (gearbox_catalog.h).

gearboxes.name: Economy 5-speed manual
gearboxes.description: Long gearing and a tall overdrive fifth for low engine speed at motorway pace. Light and efficient, built for everyday engines.

gearboxes.name: Economy 6-speed overdrive manual
gearboxes.description: Two overdrive gears, the sixth very tall. The lowest engine speed on the motorway, at the cost of punch in the top gears.

gearboxes.name: Touring 6-speed manual
gearboxes.description: The balanced six-speed of the sedans: even steps and a modest overdrive.

gearboxes.name: Close-ratio 6-speed manual
gearboxes.description: Tightly spaced gears keep the engine in its power band after every shift. Short throw, strong synchros, nearly direct sixth.

gearboxes.name: Heavy-duty 6-speed manual
gearboxes.description: Large gears and synchros for high-torque engines. Direct fourth, overdrive fifth and sixth.

gearboxes.name: Hypercar 7-speed manual
gearboxes.description: The hypercar's seven-speed: a long overdrive seventh for the top speed run and the strength for over 1,500 N*m.

gearboxes.name: Straight-cut 6-speed sequential
gearboxes.description: Racing dog box with straight-cut gears: no synchros, a sequential drum and very short shifts. Rated for the hypercar.

gearboxes.name: Vintage 3-speed sliding-mesh
gearboxes.description: Three widely spaced straight-cut gears and no synchronisers, as in the earliest motor cars. Match the speeds or it grinds.

gearboxes.name: 8-speed automatic
gearboxes.description: Torque-converter automatic with eight planetary gears: creeps away at idle, shifts on its own and locks the converter up when cruising. P R N D on the selector, the shift keys switch to manual mode.

gearboxes.name: Heavy-duty 8-speed automatic
gearboxes.description: The eight-speed automatic with a looser converter and heavier clutch packs for big-torque engines.

gearboxes.name: 7-speed dual-clutch
gearboxes.description: Two wet clutches, odd and even gears on their own shafts: the next gear waits preselected and the shift is a clutch handover in tens of milliseconds. Launches on clutch slip.

gearboxes.name: Hypercar 7-speed dual-clutch
gearboxes.description: The hypercar's gearing in a wet dual-clutch transaxle with clutches for over 1,500 N*m: near-instant shifts under full power.

gearboxes.name: CVT with torque converter
gearboxes.description: Push-belt CVT: no gears, the pulleys change the ratio steplessly so the engine holds the rpm the pedal asks for. Pulls away on a torque converter that locks up at once; in S it steps through seven fixed ratios like an automatic.

gearboxes.name: CVT with starting clutch
gearboxes.description: The push-belt CVT without a converter: a wet starting clutch slips the car away from rest and holds the variator at its launch ratio until it closes. Lighter and more direct, with less creep. In S it steps through seven fixed ratios.
